- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

input.prompt:
I need to trace how a browser request for another user's profile image (avatar) is served in this codebase — from the HTTP route handler all the way down to stored data. This is likely a web application. Search very thoroughly for:

1. Routes or handlers related to "avatar" or "profile image" or "user image" — look for URL patterns like `/avatar`, `/users/:id/avatar`, `/profile/image`, etc.
2. The handler function that serves avatar/profile images
3. Any service or middleware layer it calls
4. The data/storage layer it ultimately reads from

Search breadth: very thorough. Look in route definitions, controllers, handlers, services, repositories, and storage layers. Check for terms like "avatar", "profile_image", "user_image", "photo", "picture" in route files, handler files, and API definitions.

content.text: I now have the complete trace. Here is the full analysis. --- ## Complete Avatar Request Trace: From Browser to Stored Data This is a Go web application called **Memos** (github.com/usememos/memos), using the **Echo** HTTP framework for file serving and **gRPC-Gateway** for its API layer. The avatar data is stored as a **base64-encoded data URI** directly in the `avatar_url` column of the `user` database table. ### 1. Route Registration **File:** `/bench/repo/server/server.go` (lines 80-82) During server startup, `NewServer` creates a `FileServerService` and registers its routes on the Echo HTTP server: ```go fileServerService := fileserver.NewFileServerService(s.Profile, s.Store, s.Secret) fileServerService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer) ``` **File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 121-125) `RegisterRoutes` registers the avatar endpoint at `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar`: ```go func (s *FileServerService) RegisterRoutes(echoServer *echo.Echo) { fileGroup := echoServer.Group("/file") fileGroup.GET("/users/:identifier/avatar", s.serveUserAvatar) } ``` The endpoint is also listed as a **public method** (no authentication required on open instances) in the ACL config: **File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go` (line 25) ```go "/memos.api.v1.UserService/GetUserAvatar": {}, ``` ### 2. The Handler Function **File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 167-209) The `serveUserAvatar` method is the HTTP handler. Its logic proceeds as follows: **Step A -- Private instance authentication check (lines 173-181):** If the instance is private (no `InstanceURL` configured, meaning `Profile.AllowAnonymous()` returns false), the handler requires authentication. It calls `s.getCurrentUser()` which delegates to `Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser()`. If no valid session/token is found, it returns 401 Unauthorized. **Step B -- Look up the user by username (lines 183-191):** Extracts the `:identifier` path parameter and calls `s.getUserByUsername(ctx, identifier)` which calls: ```go s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{Username: &identifier}) ``` **Step C -- Check avatar existence (lines 192-194):** If the user's `AvatarURL` field is empty, returns 404 "avatar not found". **Step D -- Parse the data URI (lines 196-199):** Calls `s.parseDataURI(user.AvatarURL)` which uses the regex `^data:(?P[^;]+);base64,(?P.+)` to extract the MIME type and base64-decode the image data. **Step E -- Validate MIME type (lines 201-203):** Checks the parsed MIME type against `avatarAllowedTypes` (line 75): `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/jpg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`, `image/heic`, `image/heif`. **Step F -- Serve the response (lines 205-209):** Sets security headers (`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, CSP), sets `Content-Type` to the image MIME type, sets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`, and returns the decoded binary data as a blob. ### 3. Authentication / Middleware Layer **File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 708-711) `getCurrentUser` extracts the `Authorization` header and `Cookie` header and delegates to the shared `Authenticator`: ```go func (s *FileServerService) getCurrentUser(ctx context.Context, c *echo.Context) (*store.User, error) { authHeader := c.Request().Header.Get(echo.HeaderAuthorization) cookieHeader := c.Request().Header.Get("Cookie") return s.authenticator.AuthenticateToUser(ctx, authHeader, cookieHeader) } ``` **File:** `/bench/repo/server/auth/authenticator.go` (lines 190-208) `AuthenticateToUser` tries three credential types in priority order: 1. **Access Token V2** (short-lived JWT from `Authorization: Bearer `) -- stateless validation 2. **Personal Access Token (PAT)** (from `Authorization: Bearer memos_pat_...`) -- validated against the database 3. **Refresh token cookie** (fallback for browser `` tags that cannot set Authorization headers) ### 4. The Store (Service) Layer **File:** `/bench/repo/store/user.go` (lines 148-169) `Store.GetUser` first checks an in-memory cache (keyed by user ID). Since the avatar lookup is by *username* (not ID), the cache is bypassed, and it delegates to `Store.ListUsers`: ```go func (s *Store) GetUser(ctx context.Context, find *FindUser) (*User, error) { // Cache check by ID (skipped for username lookups) list, err := s.ListUsers(ctx, find) // ... user := list[0] s.userCache.Set(ctx, userCacheKey(user.ID), user) return user, nil } ``` `ListUsers` calls `s.driver.ListUsers(ctx, find)` which dispatches to the database-specific driver. The `User` struct (lines 29-45) contains the `AvatarURL` field: ```go type User struct { ID int32 RowStatus RowStatus CreatedTs int64 UpdatedTs int64 Username string Role Role Email string Nickname string PasswordHash string AvatarURL string Description string } ``` ### 5. The Database Layer **File:** `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user.go` (lines 88-205) The SQLite driver's `ListUsers` builds a query selecting from the `user` table. When the `FindUser` has `Username` set, it adds `WHERE username = ?`. The `avatar_url` column is selected and scanned into `user.AvatarURL` (line 189): ```sql SELECT id, username, role, email, nickname, password_hash, avatar_url, description, created_ts, updated_ts, row_status FROM user WHERE username = ? ``` Equivalent implementations exist for: - **PostgreSQL:** `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/user.go` (line 150 selects `avatar_url`, line 179 scans it) - **MySQL:** `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/user.go` (line 147 selects `avatar_url`, line 170 scans it) ### 6. Schema / Data Format **File:** `/bench/repo/store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql` (line 20) ```sql avatar_url TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '', ``` The avatar is stored as a **data URI** directly in the database column, e.g.: ``` data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgo... ``` This was confirmed by the test helper at `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go` (lines 443-451). ### 7. How the Frontend Gets the Avatar URL **File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go` (lines 16-41) When the API returns a `User` protobuf to the frontend, `convertUserFromStore` replaces base64 data URIs with a pointer URL to avoid sending large blobs in API responses: ```go if user.AvatarURL != "" { _, _, err := extractImageInfo(user.AvatarURL) if err == nil { userpb.AvatarUrl = fmt.Sprintf("/file/%s/avatar", userpb.Name) } else { userpb.AvatarUrl = user.AvatarURL // external URL, pass through } } ``` Here `userpb.Name` is the resource name like `users/steven`, so the resulting URL is `/file/users/steven/avatar`. If the `AvatarURL` is an external URL (not a data URI), it is passed through directly. **File:** `/bench/repo/web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx` The frontend `UserAvatar` component renders a simple `` tag pointing to whatever `avatarUrl` the API returned (either `/file/users//avatar` or an external URL). ### Summary: Complete Request Flow ``` Browser | v Echo router: GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar | v fileserver.serveUserAvatar(c) [fileserver.go:167] | +-- (private instance?) getCurrentUser() [fileserver.go:173] | | | v | Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser() [authenticator.go:190] | (checks Bearer token, then cookie) | +-- getUserByUsername(ctx, "steven") [fileserver.go:715] | | | v | Store.GetUser(&FindUser{Username: "steven"}) [user.go:148] | | | v | Store.ListUsers() [user.go:136] | | | v | driver.ListUsers() (sqlite/postgres/mysql) | | | v | SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ? | | | v | store.User{AvatarURL: "data:image/png;base64,iVBOR..."} | +-- parseDataURI(user.AvatarURL) [fileserver.go:737] | extracts MIME type + base64-decodes to []byte | +-- validate avatarAllowedTypes [fileserver.go:75] | +-- c.Blob(200, "image/png", imageData) [fileserver.go:209] sets Content-Type, Cache-Control, security headers ``` ### Key Files (all absolute paths) | Layer | File | |-------|------| | Server startup / route wiring | `/bench/repo/server/server.go` | | Route registration + HTTP handler | `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` | | Handler tests | `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go` | | Authentication logic | `/bench/repo/server/auth/authenticator.go` | | Public endpoints ACL | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go` | | API user converter (URL rewriting) | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go` | | User update (avatar validation) | `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service.go` | | Store layer (User struct + caching) | `/bench/repo/store/user.go` | | Store interface (Driver) | `/bench/repo/store/driver.go` | | SQLite driver | `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user.go` | | PostgreSQL driver | `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/user.go` | | MySQL driver | `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/user.go` | | DB schema (SQLite) | `/bench/repo/store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql` | | Profile (AllowAnonymous) | `/bench/repo/internal/profile/profile.go` | | Frontend avatar component | `/bench/repo/web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx` | | Protobuf definition | `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/user_service.proto` |

content.text: h07. A browser `` tag hits `/file/users/:identifier/avatar`. Here is each hop from handler to stored data: 1. `serveUserAvatar` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` 2. `getUserByUsername` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` 3. `Store.GetUser` — `store/user.go` 4. `Store.ListUsers` — `store/user.go` 5. `driver.ListUsers` — `store/db/sqlite/user.go` (or `store/db/postgres/user.go` / `store/db/mysql/user.go`) 6. `parseDataURI` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` **Details:** - The Echo router dispatches `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar` to `serveUserAvatar` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:167`), registered in `RegisterRoutes` at line ~121. - `serveUserAvatar` extracts the `:identifier` param (the username) and calls `getUserByUsername` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715`), which calls `s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{Username: &identifier})`. - `Store.GetUser` (`store/user.go:148`) checks an in-memory user cache (keyed by ID, so a username lookup misses), then delegates to `Store.ListUsers` (`store/user.go:136`). - `ListUsers` calls `s.driver.ListUsers(ctx, find)`, dispatching to the concrete DB driver — e.g. the SQLite implementation in `store/db/sqlite/user.go`, which runs `SELECT … avatar_url … FROM user WHERE username = ?` and scans `avatar_url` into the `User.AvatarURL` field. - Back in `serveUserAvatar`, `parseDataURI` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737`) extracts the MIME type and base64-decodes the raw image bytes from the `data:image/…;base64,…` string stored in the column. - The handler validates the MIME type against `avatarAllowedTypes` (line 75) and returns the decoded bytes via `c.Blob()`. The avatar is stored as a base64 data URI directly in the `avatar_url` TEXT column of the `user` table (schema: `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:20`).
